help.title: Help Center & User Guide
help.subtitle: Documentation, frequently asked questions, and tips to master Kyrnex
help.tip1Desc: If your project has index.html directly in the root, leave 'Public Folder' empty. Kyrnex serves assets automatically with no 404s.
help.tip2Desc: Run as many servers as you need at the same time (e.g. port 3000, 3050, and 8080) with zero interference.
help.tip3Desc: Click the ↻ button in live preview to capture an updated visual cover showing the latest web changes.

faqs.q1: My web page is in the root directory (without a 'public' folder). How do I set it up?
faqs.a1: If your files (index.html, styles.css, app.js, catalog/) live directly in the root of your project without any subfolder named 'public', simply leave the 'Public folder' field completely BLANK when creating or editing the server. Kyrnex will automatically detect that assets reside in the project root and serve them without 404 errors.
faqs.q2: What is the difference between 'Project root' and 'Public folder'?
faqs.a2: The 'Project root' is the main directory where your repository or project files live. The 'Public folder' is an optional subfolder within root (typical in Next.js, Vite, or Express MVC) where public assets are placed. If your project is flat, keep public folder blank.
faqs.q3: What happens if the configured port (e.g. 3000 or 3050) is already in use?
faqs.a3: Kyrnex features intelligent port collision handling (Auto-Fallback). If another app or background process is already using the requested port, Kyrnex will automatically find the next available port (e.g. 3051, 3052) and update the live URL dynamically.
faqs.q4: How does the live preview and reload button (↻) work?
faqs.a4: Kyrnex does not rely on heavy external browser drivers or Puppeteer. It uses Electron's native offscreen rendering technology to snap a crisp screenshot of your running app and cache it on disk. Clicking ↻ captures a fresh screenshot immediately.
faqs.q5: Why don't dismissed or read remote announcements reappear?
faqs.a5: Kyrnex uses persistent ID deduplication stored in local storage. When you mark an announcement as read or dismiss it, its identifier is remembered. You can clear this history anytime in the Settings view if you wish to re-test.
faqs.q6: My server is green (running) but shows a 'Kyrnex Local Runtime' page
faqs.a6: That is the courtesy fallback page Kyrnex displays when the server is active but cannot find your 'index.html' file. Check that 'Main file' matches your filename and that 'Public folder' is empty if the file is in the root.
faqs.q7: I changed an HTML or CSS file. Do I need to restart the server?
faqs.a7: For changes in static files (HTML, CSS, browser JS), restarting is not needed; simply refresh your browser or click ↻ on the live preview. If you modified a backend Node.js router, click the restart button on the server card.
